climate: humid subtropical; mean annual rainfall 1361 mm
cover_crop: mixed (USDA-NRCS soil health mix: cereal rye, oats, daikon radish, purple top turnips, crimson clover)
comparison: multispecies cover crop mix vs. no-cover control (no-till corn-soybean rotation)
quote: Although multispecies SHM treatment produced a 15% higher yield compared with the control in 2016, the previous yields of soybeans (in 2014) and corn (in 2013 and 2015) were not signifi­cantly different across the cover crop treatments (data not shown).
note: Soybean 2016 only. Corn yields (2013, 2015) and soybean 2014 were reported as not significantly different across cover crop treatments, but no numbers are given. The quote contains a soft hyphen at a line break in 'signifi-cantly'.

climate: humid subtropical; mean annual rainfall 1361 mm
comparison: multispecies cover crop mix vs. all other treatments incl. no-cover control
quote: Soybean yield from the multispecies SHM was signifi­cantly higher (4.55 Mg ha-1) than from all other treatments (Fig. 1d).
note: Absolute yield of the treatment; the control yield is shown only in Fig. 1d (roughly 3.96 Mg ha-1 if you back-calculate from the 15% figure). The quote contains a soft hyphen at a line break.

climate: humid subtropical; mean annual rainfall 1361 mm
comparison: cereal rye cover crop vs. no-cover control
quote: Cereal rye yield was 3.9 Mg ha-1, lower but not significantly different than the control, which could be a result of the cereal rye’s reduced N supply to the soil.
note: Soybean yield after cereal rye was numerically lower than the control but not significantly. Other single- and double-species covers were numerically higher than the control but not significantly; no values are given in the text.
